name: Community Design Regulation
impact_assessment: none (1993); evaluation SWD(2020) 264; revision IA SWD(2022) 368
evidence_rating: thin: Commission evaluation and impact assessment; independent research mostly descriptive; no causal studies
summary: The 2002 regulation created a single EU-wide design right run by the EU IP office. The Commission's 2020 evaluation found it cheaper and simpler than national routes and widely used (about 1.5 million registrations by 2019), but underused by small firms and outdated for digital designs. Its 2024 reform is forecast to save consumers EUR 340-544 million by opening up car spare parts; no independent study measures effects on innovation or prices.

indicators.objective: The 1993 proposal has no indicators section

indicators.indicator: Unitary registered and unregistered Community design administered by EUIPO
indicators.evidence: Steady growth in filings (nearly 1.5m registered Community designs 2003-2019); 2020 evaluation: registration cheaper, simpler and faster than national routes, but system underused and partly outdated for digital designs.
indicators.sources: SWD(2020) 264; EUIPO design focus report 2010-2019 (via search)

indicators.objective: Single market for products embodying designs
indicators.evidence: Broadly achieved except spare parts: 12 Member States liberalised, others keep manufacturers' monopoly; market fragmented.

indicators.objective: Spare parts liberalisation and fee cuts
indicators.indicator: Consumer savings from opening must-match spare parts market; fee savings
indicators.target_or_baseline: EUR 340-544m consumer savings after 10 years; EUR 6m/yr fee savings

literature.citation: European Commission (2020), Evaluation of EU legislation on design protection (executive summary SWD(2020) 265), SWD(2020) 264
literature.title: Evaluation of EU legislation on design protection (executive summary SWD(2020) 265)
literature.outcomes: access to protection; single market; costs
literature.headline: Broadly fit for purpose; unitary registration lowered costs, complexity and delays; benefits outweigh costs; but system underused (lack of awareness), not adapted to digital designs, spare parts market fragmented, fees and procedures create unnecessary burden
literature.summary_plain: The Commission's 2020 review found the EU design right works well and is cheaper than national routes, but is underused and out of date for digital designs.

literature.citation: European Commission (2022), Impact assessment on the revision of EU design legislation (executive summary SWD(2022) 369), SWD(2022) 368
literature.title: Impact assessment on the revision of EU design legislation (executive summary SWD(2022) 369)
literature.headline: Design-intensive industries almost 16% of EU GDP and 14% of jobs (2014-2016); liberalising spare parts to save consumers EUR 340-544m once fully phased in; lower fees save EUR 6m a year; simpler procedures EUR 1.6m a year
literature.summary_plain: The Commission expected its design-law reform to save consumers EUR 340-544 million by opening up the car spare-parts market.

literature.citation: Filitz, Henkel & Tether (2015), Protecting aesthetic innovations? An exploration of the use of registered community designs, Research Policy 44(6)
literature.title: Protecting aesthetic innovations? An exploration of the use of registered community designs
literature.method: exploratory qualitative (German firms in footwear, cars, tool-making) plus filing statistics
literature.headline: About three-quarters of a million RCDs filed in the first decade; firms use RCDs in very different ways across industries; little prior empirical research on design rights
literature.summary_plain: A study of German firms found registered Community designs are widely used but in very different ways across industries, and that their economic effects are barely studied.
